BiblicalUsage: Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pound weight, for the burial of Jesus. The word is the compound itself, and John names it at the burial, where the spices were the last honour given to the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I take Nicodemus's mixture as the measure of his love: a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes, brought in the night, for the body of the Lord.
